practice.title: Charla: la fuerza de los lazos débiles (≈ 190 palabras)

segments.text: In sociology, there's a concept called the 'strength of weak ties'. Most people assume that our closest friends are the most useful when we look for a job. But in the 1970s, the sociologist Mark Granovetter interviewed workers in Boston and found something surprising.

Most of them had found their jobs through acquaintances, people they saw only occasionally, rather than through close friends. Why? Because close friends tend to know the same people and the same information as we do. Acquaintances, on the other hand, belong to different networks, so they can introduce us to opportunities we would never hear about otherwise.

This doesn't mean close friends are unimportant. They provide emotional support, which weak ties rarely do. But when the goal is to find new information, a wide network of casual contacts is often more valuable. So, the next time you attend a conference or a campus event, remember that a brief conversation with a stranger could open a door.
